notes: Dated checkpoints. tools/check_review_dates.py fails after a date passes, so the weekly workflow opens an issue and a person re-checks the sources. A checkpoint is a prompt to re-read sources, not a prediction that anything will change. Remove or move a checkpoint only after doing the work, and say so in CHANGELOG.md.

checkpoints.what: Source review: check every Utah page against its sources. The Utah guide was researched on Nov. 10, 2026 through a tool that answers questions about a page instead of returning its full text (docs/research-log.md); each source was accessed and reviewed against the facts it supports, and the registry shows which were read in full. Start with the numbers people act on: 90 and 15 days for hearings (U19), 30 days for the verification form (U04), 10 days for requested items (U16), the Jan. 1, 2027 date for tribal status proof (U28), and every phone, fax, and mailing address. When it is done, remove the 'This guide is new' box from the Utah About page and the 'How we read Utah's' line from the Utah Every source page (claim U-NEW-GUIDE), or reword them to record the completed source review.

Washington: source review of the Washington guide (the list is in docs/research-log.md). The guide merged on Nov. 12, 2026 ahead of this review, on the project owner's direction. The guide was built on Nov. 12, 2026 from a research dossier, and 14 of its 25 sources are marked 'opened': false. Read WA22 (the work requirements client page and its screener) first, then WA05 at its own HCA address, compared line by line with the copy the research read; then WA21 and its code list, WA12, WA13, the five WAC sections (WA15 to WA19), WA20, WA23, WA14 at item 62, and the WA25 caption. For each one read, set 'opened' to true and the 'checked' date, and remove 'Drafting claim' from the notes of the claims it supports. Then settle the open points in docs/corrections.md (Washington items 1 to 12), starting with whether hours at a paid job are a way to meet the rule by themselves (item 2), which decides step 3 of the check. When it is done, reword the 'This guide is new' box on the Washington About page, the 'Not finished' line on the Washington Every source page, and the two warning boxes on washington-denied.html and washington-health.html.

Washington, 30-day re-check: re-read HCA's client pages (WA01, WA02, WA22) and its stakeholder page (WA03) for any change to the Jan. 1, 2027 start, and for any word on a delay; the guide says nothing about a delay of the start, and stays that way until an official source speaks (the federal hold harmless option of Nov. 13, 2026 is not a delay of the start and has its own checkpoint, 2026-12-11). Re-read WA23: Apple Health Expansion enrollment was closed as of December 2025, and the immigration page must not send people to a closed program as if it were open. Check the Attorney General's tracker (WA14) and the docket (S40) for an appeal or a new order. Look for the sources not yet found: HCA's August 2026 eligibility training material, any WAC rulemaking for H.R. 1, any state plan amendment or waiver request, the work requirements notice HCA sends clients, and the list of fact sheet languages behind WA-HLP-03.

30-day re-check for Oregon and Utah (Washington's is the 2026-12-09 checkpoint). Oregon: re-check OHA's pages (S01, S03, S07, and S24 by hand) for any response to the Oct. 29, 2026 court ruling; they had none on Nov. 10. Utah: re-check U01, U02, U03, and U04 for the same, and for form 742 and the medically frail screener being posted. Court: check the docket (S40) for a notice of appeal or any new order after the Oct. 29, 2026 judgment; none appeared through the Nov. 6 entries. Update C-COURT and U-COURT and their 'As of' dates on reasons.html, health.html, utah-reasons.html, and utah-health.html.

Hold harmless period (S41, SMD# 26-006): Dec. 11, 2026 is the date by which a state that intends to use the period from Jan. 1, 2027 was asked to notify CMS. It is not a date for a public announcement. Search each state's pages again for its choice: Oregon S07 (and S24 by hand), K13, and OHA's news releases; Utah U01, U02, U04, U24, and Utah Medicaid's news page; Washington WA01, WA03, WA22, and HCA's news list. Check medicaid.gov for a later letter or a list of states. If nothing has changed, update the 'As of' date in C-HH-STATE, U-HH-STATE, and WA-HH-05 and on each guide's home, rules, and turned-down pages, and set a new checkpoint. If a state has announced its choice from an official source, register that source, reword that state's claims and pages, and reword the start and coverage-loss claims listed here. Update Washington item 7 in docs/corrections.md either way.

Before the Jan. 1, 2027 switch: re-read S01 (Oregon) and U02 (Utah) for any change to past medical bills (retroactive coverage). Then run python3 tools/check_review_dates.py --today 2027-01-02 and confirm the only expired notes it names are the Dec. 31 notes on index.html (2), bills.html (1), washington.html (2), washington-bills.html (1), utah.html (2), and utah-bills.html (1). Washington: re-read WA01 and WA03 for the same.

After Jan. 1, 2027: delete the elements marked data-show-until="2026-12-31" on index.html, bills.html, washington.html, washington-bills.html, utah.html, and utah-bills.html, so readers without JavaScript stop seeing them. Reword every guide's home page title and headline ('New rules start Jan. 1, 2027') for a site read after the rules began. Utah: the letter on tribal status (U28) asked for proof by Jan. 1, 2027; check what Utah now says to people who have not sent it, and update U-AIAN-PROOF.

First check after the rules start. Oregon: re-read S01 to S09 and S24 by hand. Look for new OHA notices, forms (including any new version of OHP 7210), and any change to the 35-day reply window. Utah: re-read U01 to U05 and U14 to U16. Look for a new 61MED that asks about the rules, form 742, the medically frail screener, and what Utah's denial and verification letters are called. If form 742 or the screener is posted, update the 'what to do' lines in site/assets/js/checker-utah.js, docs/checker-logic.md, and U-742-NOLINK. Washington: re-read WA01, WA05, and WA22. HCA said in 2026 that there was nothing to do 'right now'; that line (WA-HOME-02) is out of date once HCA changes it, so reword every place the guide repeats it, including site/assets/js/checker-washington.js. The rules reach a person at their first renewal in 2027 (WA-HOME-03); decide whether the Washington guide needs renewal pages.
Utah: DWS says the rules reach current members at reviews for renewals due in March 2027 or later (U04). Re-read U04 and U13, and decide whether the Utah guide needs renewal pages.

End of the court's six-month bar on penalizing plaintiff states (S28). Re-check the health reason and the case docket for appeals or new orders. Washington is a plaintiff state too: re-check WA14 and the two court notes on washington-reasons.html and washington-health.html.
Utah: the glossary (U08) says Targeted Adult Medicaid ends June 30, 2027 and its members move to Adult Expansion Medicaid. Re-read U08, U25, and U26, and update every Utah page that names TAM.

June 30, 2027 is the last day a state's hold harmless period can cover (S41). Reword or remove the 'A new choice for states' update box on each guide's home page and the matching parts of the rules and turned-down pages, for a site read after the period. A state may have picked a shorter time; if so, do this at that state's end date instead.
Prepare for more frequent renewals in late 2027. Decide whether to add renewal pages for people who are now members.
Prepare for 2028 proof rules. Replace 'In 2027, no doctor's note is needed' with current OHA guidance.
